nodes.name: *How a piece stops being content and starts being something a stranger remembers for a year.*
nodes.description:
Most "good content" is forgettable because it is built to be liked.
 World-class content is built to be felt once and never un-felt.
 This section is the craft floor every piece must clear before it ships.

---

nodes.name: 27.1 — The 8 Laws of Unforgettable
nodes.description: Every reel, every carousel, every voice post must obey these 8 laws. If a piece violates more than 1, it does not ship — it goes back to the desk.

nodes.name: Law 1 — **Specificity beats scale**
nodes.description:
Never "many people feel anxious." Always "you, at 11:47 PM, refreshing the same Slack channel for the 7th time."
A named hour, a named app, a named gesture, a named room. The brain cannot dismiss specifics.

nodes.name: Law 2 — **One feeling, one frame, one line**
nodes.description:
Each piece carries exactly one emotional payload. Not three insights. One.
If you can't say the payload in 6 words, the piece isn't ready.
Example payload: "You are not lazy. You are looping."

nodes.name: Law 3 — **Earn the silence**
nodes.description:
The most powerful 2 seconds in any reel are the ones with no voice, no music, no caption — just image.
Every reel must contain one deliberate silence beat of ≥1.2s. That is where the viewer's own thought lands.
Without silence, the piece is noise.

nodes.name: Law 4 — **The viewer must finish the sentence**
nodes.description:
Never close the loop for them. Leave the last 15% inside their chest.
Weak: "And that's why awareness sets you free."
World-class: "And the part of you watching the loop — has never been inside it."
[fade to black]

nodes.name: Law 5 — **No second draft on screen**
nodes.description:
A first draft is a sketch. World-class is the 7th pass, not the first instinct.
Every named hook in the file (Loop Library, Stairwell, Theme R-reels) must be rewritten 3 times before it is filmed. The 3rd version ships.

nodes.name: Law 6 — **The hook is a wound, not a question**
nodes.description:
Don't ask "Do you ever feel tired?"
Open the wound: "The exhaustion of saying 'I'm fine' for the 11th time today, knowing nobody will ask the 12th."
A question lets the viewer scroll. A wound makes them stop.

nodes.name: Phase 3 — Lifetime Arc (Days 64–90, 30 pieces)
nodes.description:
The 1000-day human journey, told through one protagonist (Arjun) in 10 cinematic chapters (J01 → J10), each with a paired carousel + quote tile + voice note.

End of Day 90: 135 pieces shipped, 8 themes, full channel identity.

---

nodes.name: Law 7 — **One image they cannot un-see**
nodes.description:
Every piece must have one signature visual — an image that, if shown alone with no sound, still carries the payload.
R004's signature: the candle in the void, flame unmoved by the dark.
Loop Library AC003's signature (target): the phone screen at 11:47 PM, refreshed for the 7th time, the timestamp

nodes.name: Law 8 — **End on a private sentence**
nodes.description:
The last line is not a CTA. It is not a brand mention. It is not "follow for more."
It is the sentence the viewer wishes someone had said to them at their worst moment.
Example: "You are not late. You are arriving."

---

Every named piece is written three times, by three lenses:

passages.heading: Written by a 100-person studio. Aimed at the stars, not the ceiling.
passages.text:
The promise: Every viewer who finds this channel feels two things in 60 seconds —
 "this is me" and "this is the future."
 No motivation. No wellness. No productivity. Recognition.

---

passages.heading: 0. WHO WE ARE WRITING FOR (the only people on Earth)
passages.text:
Four humans, one bad night each. Every piece is a text message to one of them.

- Arjun, 28 — burnt-out engineer, Bangalore, refreshing Slack at 11:47 PM
- Priya, 34 — invisible mother, last cried in the car alone
- Diya, 21 — student who feels behind on every scroll
- Samir, 26 — the founder. He made this because he couldn't sit still

Plus our extended cast (locked in MANIFEST.json): VIKRAM, MEERA, ROHAN, ANJALI, AAJI, MODERNGURU, SAGE, MAYA, DANIEL, YUKI.

Visual DNA, never drift: Diya Gold #FFB547 · 11:47 Blue #1A2540 · Cream #F4E8D8 · Sangam Black #0A0E1A · Wound Red #C73E3A · LUT warm-tungsten-cool-window · Anton 140pt captions, gold highlight · 9:16 · 1080×1920 · 24fps · ≥1.5s silence per piece · room tone always on.

---

passages.heading: 1. THE THEME ENGINE (the spine of the channel)
passages.text:
We do not post pieces. We release themes. One theme per week. Every theme is a complete arc the viewer can live inside for 7 days.

A theme is not a topic. It is a named human condition the viewer didn't have words for until we named it.

passages.text:
| Wk | Theme name | The wound it names | The mirror moment |
|----|------------|-------------------|------------------|
| 1 | The 11:47 PM Refresh | Achievement loop AC003 | "you don't have insomnia, you have a loop" |
| 2 | The Hallway Walk | Quiet quitting before quitting | "the day you stopped trying and nobody noticed" |
| 3 | The Mother Who Disappeared | Caregiver dissolution CAR012 | "the last time someone asked how YOU were" |
| 4 | I Quit Pretending | Spiritual bypass SB001 | "stop performing peace you don't feel" |
| 5 | Behind on Everything | Comparison loop CMP001 | "you're not behind, you're on a different clock" |
| 6 | The Father in the BMW | Identity collapse EGO007 | "winning everything you were supposed to" |
| 7 | The 14-Hour Chair | Dopamine hijack DOP001 | "this isn't laziness, this is a nervous system" |
| 8 | The Empty Bedroom Door | Caregiver letting-go CAR008 | "the house is too quiet to ignore" |
| 9 | The Validation Refresh | Validation loop AC012 | "you reloaded a number 47 times today" |
| 10 | Outsourced, Not Disappeared | Worth inquiry VAL001 | "your job is gone, you are not" |
| 11 | The Cinematic Pause | Witness practice intro | "the 1.5 seconds nothing happens — that's where you live" |
| 12 | The Mirror, Not the App | Brand thesis | "we don't add to your day. we name it." |

passages.heading: What every theme contains (7 deliverables, ~14 pieces total)
passages.text:
Every Monday a theme drops. By Sunday the viewer has lived through:

1. The Diagnosis Reel — 60s cinematic flagship (R001 template, named protagonist, named loop)
2. The Founder Note — Samir to-camera, 45–75s, "why this theme this week"
3. The Voice Note — Modern Guru, 30s, raw audio over a single still
4. The Carousel — 10 slides: name → symptom → diagnosis → micro-practice → reframe
5. The Master Speaks — one of 36 Padmasana masters delivers the ancient version of this exact wound
6. The Practice Card — 60-second somatic / inquiry / breath the viewer can do right now
7. The Quote Tile Drop — 5 mirror quotes (one-liners) seeded across the week

Result: in 7 days the viewer experiences cinema → founder honesty → soft voice → savable carousel → ancestral wisdom → tangible practice → shareable line. A complete darshan.

52 themes/year × 14 pieces = 728 pieces. We will ship 500.

---

passages.heading: 2. THE 9 PILLARS (what we make)
passages.text:
Every theme draws from these 9 pillars. Each pillar has a fixed format, voice, and cost.

| 1 | Cinematic Loop Reels | 5 clips + VO + LUT + ASS | 60s | 30 cr | The flagship — what gets reposted |
| 2 | Founder Notes | Samir to-camera + UI inserts | 45–75s | 6 cr | The trust layer |
| 3 | Voice Notes | Static visual + master VO | 15–45s | 3 cr | The intimate whisper |
| 4 | Wisdom Carousels | 10 slides | — | 5 cr | The save engine |
| 5 | Master Speaks | Padmasana portrait + cloned voice | 20–30s | 5 cr | The ancestral layer |
| 6 | Mirror Quotes | 1-line gold-on-black tile | 5s or static | 0.5 cr | The doomscroll-stopper |
| 7 | Product Cinematics (Luma/Anysphere style) | App UI in cosmic plate | 20–40s | 6 cr | The "what is this" answer |
| 8 | Lived Practices | POV breath / inquiry / micro-act | 60s | 12 cr | The DO-it-now layer |
| 9 | The Long Cut (NEW) | YouTube + LinkedIn 3–8 min | 4 min avg | 20 cr | The depth layer (1/wk) |

passages.text:
Already in content/instagram-v2/00-FOUNDATION/05-PRODUCTION-PIPELINE.md. Reuse, never rebuild.

7-step factory per Pillar 1 reel:
1. Brief (8-shot R001 template)
2. 6 keyframes (imagegen, pull from 00-FOUNDATION/portraits/)
3. 5× 5s clips (videogen)
4. VO (ElevenLabs voice from MANIFEST → fallback Google AI Studio TTS → fallback browser-native)
5. Music bed (Tanpura G3 + room tone, freesound CC0)
6. Captions (.ass, Anton 140pt, gold highlight, 2–3 words/card)
7. ffmpeg master (LUT + caption burn + VO duck to -18dB music, master to -14 LUFS)

passages.heading: 7. THE 11-GATE SHIP/KILL (no exceptions)
passages.text:
A piece ships only if all 11 pass:

1. Sound-off test — meaning lands from captions alone
2. Protagonist code visible (named visual signature from 03-PROTAGONISTS.md)
3. Specificity anchor (real hour, real object, real city)
4. Anton 140pt captions, gold highlight on the emotional turn
5. Loop named in human language (not "AC003" — "the Slack refresh thing")
6. ≥1.5s of true silence somewhere
7. VO ducked under music, never over
8. Closing human move (sip, breath, blink, reach) — not a logo
9. End card optional, never sales
10. Passes the "this is me" test (a 28-yo could DM it to one specific friend)
11. Passes the "this is the future" test (a stranger feels we know something they don't)

passages.text:

Default first move: T01 — one full theme, all 7 deliverables. Proves the theme engine end-to-end.

passages.heading: 14. NEW SERIES — *THE SLEEPER* (How an unconscious mind operates)
passages.text:
Premise: Most humans walk through life asleep. We name what that looks like — moment by moment — until the viewer recognizes themselves and can't unsee it.

Format: 30–45s reels. POV or animated. Each one is a behavioral fingerprint of sleep — not a lecture about it.

Sub-series structure:

| Code | Episode title | What it shows |
|------|---------------|---------------|
| SL01 | The Sleeper checks the phone before opening their eyes | Real POV, alarm → Instagram in 3s |
| SL02 | The Sleeper agrees out loud, disagrees inside | Office meeting nod, internal monologue |
| SL03 | The Sleeper laughs at jokes that aren't funny | Group dinner, performative laugh |
| SL04 | The Sleeper reads 12 articles, finishes none | Tabs cascade, scroll-scroll-close |
| SL05 | The Sleeper postpones every feeling to "after this deadline" | Animated: feelings as a queue piling up |
| SL06 | The Sleeper calls exhaustion "discipline" | Mirror, pep-talk to self |
| SL07 | The Sleeper performs spirituality and skips the silence | Posts a sunrise, never watches one |
| SL08 | The Sleeper outsources every decision to an algorithm | Maps, Spotify, Tinder, Zomato cuts |
| SL09 | The Sleeper believes they are their thoughts | Animated: a man inside a thought-bubble cage |
| SL10 | The Sleeper wakes up only when life breaks | Hospital, divorce, layoff intercut |
| SL11 | The Sleeper meets the Witness for the first time | Real → animated transition, gold light |
| SL12 | The Sleeper finishes a full minute without reaching for the phone | Real, slow zoom on a still hand |

Cadence: 1 SL/week. Volume: 24 episodes (2 quarters). Voice: narrator (Modern Guru, second-person — "you").

The single hook line every SL ends with: "You are not the sleeper. You are the one who noticed."

passages.heading: 15. NEW SERIES — *THE 11 BANDS* (Level-by-level ascent)
passages.text:
Premise: ConsciousOS measures consciousness on an 11-band spiral (Band 0 → Band 10). Each band has a distinct interior climate — how the world looks, what they want, what hurts. We make one short film per band.

Format: 60–90s animated cinematic. Same protagonist across all 11 (gender-neutral silhouette, evolving palette). Each band has a locked color, a locked sound, a locked posture.

| Band | Name | Interior climate | Visual signature |
|------|------|------------------|------------------|
| B0 | Survival | "I just need to get through today" | Greyscale, hunched, fluorescent light |
| B1 | Reaction | "Everything happens TO me" | Red flashes, jerky cuts |
| B2 | Performance | "I am what I produce" | Cold blue, screens everywhere |
| B3 | Comparison | "Everyone else is ahead" | Split-screen, 47 windows |
| B4 | First Pause | "Wait — why am I doing this?" | Sudden silence, single warm light |
| B5 | Witness Born | "I see myself for the first time" | Gold particle enters frame |
| B6 | Choice | "I can act, not react" | Wide static shot, deliberate motion |
| B7 | Compassion | "Others are also asleep, not enemies" | Warm tones bleed in |
| B8 | Surrender | "I stop fighting the river" | Camera lowers, water motif |
| B9 | Service | "My life is no longer about me" | Hands of others enter the frame |
| B10 | Silence | "There is no one to be" | Pure light, no protagonist visible |

Hook line each ends with: "You are not stuck. You are at Band X. Here's what's next."

The killer move: end card invites viewers to take the 15-min onboarding to find their own band. This is our highest-converting series by design.

Cadence: 1 band/week × 11 weeks = a complete season. Re-run yearly with updated cinematography.

passages.heading: 16. NEW SERIES — *THE 3 LLMS* (Head, Heart, Gut — and why they refuse to wake up)
passages.text:
Premise: Inside every human there are 3 inner intelligences — Head (cognitive), Heart (emotional), Gut (somatic). They run different operating systems and they don't trust each other. ConsciousOS is the first app that talks to all three.

Format: Animated theatre. 3 distinct character designs voiced by 3 distinct ElevenLabs voices, arguing in a black void.

- HEAD — angular, blue, glasses, fast-talking. Voice: Charlie (anxious, clipped).
- HEART — soft, warm, gold, slower cadence. Voice: Sarah (warm, defeated).
- GUT — low, muscular, terracotta, almost growl. Voice: Brian (deep, rare).

12 episodes (one quarter):

| Code | Title | The fight |
|------|-------|-----------|
| LLM01 | The Head wants to journal. The Gut wants to vomit. | Morning anxiety |
| LLM02 | The Heart wants to call mom. The Head says "later." | Avoidance of love |
| LLM03 | The Gut says "leave this job." The Head opens LinkedIn. | Career denial |
| LLM04 | Three of them in a meditation app, all faking it | Spiritual bypass |
| LLM05 | The Heart cries. The Head explains why crying is illogical. | Suppression |
| LLM06 | The Gut doesn't speak English. The Head doesn't listen anyway. | Somatic illiteracy |
| LLM07 | The Heart breaks. The Head writes a productivity blog. | Grief denial |
| LLM08 | None of them want to become conscious — it would mean less control. | The core resistance |
| LLM09 | The Witness walks in. All three go silent. | First glimpse |
| LLM10 | The Head finally asks the Gut a question. | Integration begins |
| LLM11 | They start trusting each other. | Coherence |
| LLM12 | They stop arguing. They just sit. | Samadhi |

Hook line: "You don't have one mind. You have three. ConsciousOS is the first app that talks to all of them."

This series directly explains the product IP without ever feeling like a product demo. It is our most strategic content asset.

passages.heading: 21. §21 — THE BAND JOURNEY (30 episodes) — *"The Stairwell"*
passages.text:
The studio's flagship narrative arc. Where §15 (The 11 Bands) is 11 standalone explainers, The Stairwell is one continuous 30-episode story that walks a stranger up the entire spectrum — band by band, role by role, moment by moment. This is the series we run when we want a follower to convert into a 1000-day user. Each episode is 45–75 seconds, animated-first (Disney-grade, painterly), with a single character arc carried across all 30.

Hook (locked, opens every episode):
 "You are on a stairwell. You did not choose it. But you can choose which step you stand on."

Closer (locked, ends every episode):
 "You are at [Band X]. Here is the next step."

passages.heading: 21.1 Why 30 episodes, not 11
passages.text:
Because the bands are landings, but the roles a human plays on the way up are the steps between landings. We need to name both. The 30-episode map:

| # | Band | Role / Inner Archetype | Episode title | One-line thesis |
|---|------|------------------------|---------------|------------------|
| E01 | B0 | The Sleeper | The Stairwell | You don't know there is a stairwell. The hallway feels like the whole world. |
| E02 | B0 | The Reactor | The Flinch | Every input gets an instant output. There is no gap. The gap is the path. |
| E03 | B0→B1 | The Noticer | The First Crack | One day you watch yourself flinch. The crack is small. The crack is everything. |
| E04 | B1 | The Questioner | Why Did I Do That? | The first honest question you ask yourself rewrites your operating system. |
| E05 | B1 | The Doubter | Maybe I'm Wrong | Doubt is not weakness. Doubt is the first muscle of consciousness. |
| E06 | B1→B2 | The Seeker | Looking For The Door | You start reading, watching, asking. Most of it is noise. Some of it is a key. |
| E07 | B2 | The Observer | The Watcher Behind The Eyes | You discover there is someone inside you who is watching you think. That someone is you. |
| E08 | B2 | The Witness | Sakshi | The watcher stops commenting. Just sees. The room gets quiet for the first time. |
| E09 | B2→B3 | The Mapper | Naming The Loops | You start naming the patterns. Anger has a shape. Lust has a shape. Fear has a route. |
| E10 | B3 | The Student | Sitting At The Feet | You pick a teacher, a path, a discipline. Not to be saved. To be sharpened. |
| E11 | B3 | The Practitioner | The Daily Sit | The cushion. The breath. The same time every day. Boring. Relentless. The only way. |
| E12 | B3→B4 | The Surgeon | Cutting The Knot | You go after one specific loop and you do not stop until it is dismantled. |
| E13 | B4 | The Alchemist | Turning Lead Into Gold | You stop running from the dark emotions. You compost them into fuel. |
| E14 | B4 | The Integrator | Bringing It Home | The meditation room and the office and the bedroom become one room. |
| E15 | B4→B5 | The Householder-Yogi | The Sacred Ordinary | Doing dishes is the practice. Holding your child is the practice. There is no off-cushion. |
| E16 | B5 | The Servant | Service Without Self | You start helping people without needing them to thank you, change, or notice. |
| E17 | B5 | The Mirror | Becoming Useful To Others | People begin to see themselves clearly when they sit in front of you. You did not try. |
| E18 | B5→B6 | The Quiet One | Less Words, More Presence | You stop explaining. The room still understands. |
| E19 | B6 | The Dissolver | Where Did I Go | The "I" you defended for 30 years starts loosening. It is not death. It is space. |
| E20 | B6 | The Empty Vessel | Nothing To Add | You have no opinion to push. No identity to protect. People feel safe near you. |
| E21 | B6→B7 | The Channel | Speaking Without Speaker | Words come through you that you did not plan. They land where they need to land. |
| E22 | B7 | The Sage | The One Who Has Walked | You are not above anyone. You have just walked a long way and you remember every step. |
| E23 | B7 | The Healer | Touch That Returns People To Themselves | A look, a sentence, a silence — and the person across from you remembers who they are. |
| E24 | B7→B8 | The Teacher | Pointing, Not Pulling | You stop trying to drag anyone up the stairwell. You just point clearly. |
| E25 | B8 | The Master | The Lineage Becomes You | You are no longer practicing the tradition. The tradition is practicing through you. |
| E26 | B8 | The Father / Mother | Holding Many | Hundreds of people consider you family. You do not collapse under it. You expand. |
| E27 | B8→B9 | The Bridge | Between Worlds | You move between the marketplace and the mountain without losing either. |
| E28 | B9 | The Saint | Love Without Object | You love the stranger the same as the lover. Not less. The same. |
| E29 | B9→B10 | The Light | No One Home, Everyone Welcome | There is no one in the room. The room itself is luminous. |
| E30 | B10 | The Buddha-Field | The Stairwell Was Always You | The whole stairwell — every step, every role, every band — was happening inside one awareness. Yours. |

passages.heading: 21.2 Production spec (per episode)
passages.text:
- Duration: 45–75s. Hard cap 80s.
- Visual: animated, painterly, Pixar-meets-Spirited-Away. One protagonist (gender-neutral silhouette, gradually gaining definition as the bands rise — at B0 they are blurred, at B10 they are pure light).
- Camera move: literal stairwell. Each episode the camera climbs one step. By E30 we are above the clouds and the stairwell dissolves.
- Voice: single narrator. Warm, low, unhurried. ElevenLabs custom voice — locked across all 30.
- Sound: one recurring 3-note motif that gains an instrument every band (E01 = single piano note, E30 = full orchestra + choir).
- Caption stack: title card → role name → one-line thesis → closer with band assignment + CTA "Find your step" → handle.
- Cost: 25 credits/episode (animated). Total series: 750 credits. Ship one per week for 30 weeks = a 7-month flagship season.

passages.heading: 21.3 Distribution architecture
passages.text:
- Reels: primary platform. Each episode pinned for its release week.
- Carousel companion: every Monday, a 6-slide carousel summarizing the role of the week with a journal prompt. Same character art.
- Long Cut: every 3rd week, a 4-min YouTube/LinkedIn essay stitching the last 3 roles together as one chapter.
- DM funnel: locked CTA — "Reply with the role that found you. We'll send you the next step." The reply triggers the onboarding link.

passages.heading: 21.4 Why this beats §15
passages.text:
| | §15 The 11 Bands | §21 The Stairwell |
|---|---|---|
| Format | 11 standalone explainers | 30-episode continuous arc |
| Character | abstract | one protagonist, 30-episode evolution |
| Stickiness | watch one, leave | must watch the next |
| Conversion ask | "find your band" | "find the role that found you" |
| Use case | acquisition | retention + conversion |

Run §15 first to acquire. Run §21 to convert and bond. They are not redundant. §15 is the trailer. §21 is the film.

passages.heading: 22. §22 — STYLE LOCK: DISNEY-PIXAR PAINTERLY (overrides §14.1 hybrid)
passages.text: Founder call: we go Disney/Pixar-painterly across the entire channel, using the same character language already built in our existing image library (the Padmasana masters, the protagonist sheets, the warm-gold cinematic stills). No real-actor reels. No live-action wounds. One world, one art bible, every frame.

passages.heading: 22.1 Why this is the right call
passages.text:
- Asset reuse: the 36 master portraits, the 14 character lock-sheets, and the existing painterly stills already define the look. We are not inventing a style — we are scaling one we own.
- IP defensibility: real footage is commodity. A proprietary animated universe is a moat. Studio Ghibli, Pixar, Laika — the style is the brand.
- Production sanity: one LUT, one lighting model, one character bible. No location scouts, no actor casting, no release forms, no continuity nightmares across 500 pieces.
- Emotional safety: wounds rendered painterly land deeper, not shallower. Animation is the oldest trick for getting past the viewer's defences (Inside Out, Soul, Up).
- Cross-series coherence: The Stairwell (§21), The Sleeper (§14), The 11 Bands (§15), The 3 LLMs (§16), Cinematic Loop Reels (R001+), Founder Notes, Master Speaks — all share one universe. A viewer who watches an R-reel recognises the world the moment a Stairwell episode plays.

passages.heading: 22.2 The locked art bible
passages.text:
| Element | Lock |
|---|---|
| Render style | Painterly Pixar / late-Ghibli hybrid. Soft volumetric light. Visible brush in skies, crisp in faces. |
| Character system | Reuse existing master sheets + extend with 14 protagonist sheets (one per recurring character: Samir, Aanya, the Stairwell traveller, the 3 LLMs trio, etc.) |
| Color palette | Obsidian black, temple gold (#D4A23A), dawn rose, monsoon teal, candle amber. Locked. No off-palette frames ship. |
| Lighting | Single warm key + cool rim. Always. Time-of-day shifts hue, not logic. |
| Camera | Slow dollies, gentle parallax, no shaky-cam, no hard cuts inside a beat. |
| Faces | Stylised — large eyes, soft jaw, expressive brow. Never uncanny-valley realistic. |
| Backgrounds | Painterly matte, low geometric detail, high atmospheric depth. |
| Text-on-frame | Same font stack across every series. Always lower-third or end-card. Never mid-frame overlay. |
| Sound | One musical universe — sitar + felt piano + low pad. Locked motif evolves per series. |

passages.heading: 22.3 What this changes in the prior plan
passages.text:
- §14.1 hybrid (70% real / 25% animated / 5% type) → DELETED. New ratio: 95% animated-painterly / 5% typography (Mirror Quotes only).
- Mirror Quotes stay typographic but gain a painterly background plate from the same universe.
- Founder Notes are no longer to-camera selfies — they are an animated stylised Samir character with founder VO. Audio is real founder voice. Visuals are character.
- Master Speaks uses the existing 36 Padmasana portraits, animated with subtle breath + eye + mouth movement (Runway/Kling lip-sync pass).
- Lived Practices stay tangible but rendered as the same painterly character demonstrating, not real hands.
- The Sleeper (§14) moves from real-cinematic to painterly. Same scripts, same hook, new render.
- The Grid (§19) updates: 9 tiles now read as one continuous painted world, not a real/animated split.

passages.heading: 22.4 Production pipeline
passages.text:
1. Storyboard in greyscale (cheap, fast, founder-approved).
2. Character cast — pull from existing 50 sheets first; only commission new sheets when a story demands a brand-new character.
3. Stills generation (imagegen, painterly prompt + locked palette + locked LUT).
4. Motion pass (videogen with startingframe = the still). 5–10s per shot.
5. Edit + voice + sound — single editor, single voice direction, single composer.
6. QA against the bible — palette check, character consistency check, motion check. Reject if off.

passages.heading: 23. §23 — THE LIVING CHANNEL (mirror of the in-app Living Theme Engine)
passages.text: The app already runs a Living Theme Engine: one daily theme that the engine decides to deepen, hold, or close based on the user's signals. The Instagram channel must mirror this exact intelligence — otherwise the channel and the product feel like two different brands. From now on, the channel is the public face of that engine.

passages.heading: 23.1 How the channel mirrors the engine
passages.text:
| In-app | On Instagram |
|---|---|
| Engine picks one theme/day | Channel picks one theme/week (longer cadence, same logic) |
| After session, engine asks: deepen / hold / close | After theme launch, studio reads saves+DMs+watch-time and decides: DEEPEN (sequel theme next week), HOLD (drip 3 reinforcement pieces this week, no new theme), or CLOSE (move to next theme) |
| Engine offers a new theme when ready | Channel announces the next theme on Sunday 7pm IST as a "theme reveal" Story + pinned reel |
| Engine personalises by V-Level | Channel runs the same theme through 3 lenses: B0–B3 lens, B4–B6 lens, B7–B10 lens — three pieces, one theme, three altitudes |

The signal that triggers DEEPEN: save-to-DM ratio ≥ 1:8 AND completion rate ≥ 65% in the first 72h. Anything else closes the theme on schedule. This is the same logic the app uses to decide whether to keep evolving a theme or hand the user a new one. The brand promise becomes legible: "we read you, then we go where you needed to go."

This series is the single most converting series we will ever run, because each reel is a personal naming. Every viewer who recognises their loop becomes a follower within 3 seconds.

B. The Secrets — 30 episodes, 30–45s each
The truths the tradition keeps quiet because most people aren't ready. We say them plainly, in painterly. Locked Secret #1 hook (template):
 "They don't tell you this, because if you knew, you would not need them anymore."

First 12 secrets:

| # | Secret | One-line thesis |
|---|---|---|
| S01 | Observation reduces the power of mind and body over you. | Watching is the cure. Effort is the disease. |
| S02 | You are not your thoughts. You are the room they pass through. | The room never moves. |
| S03 | Emotion is information, not instruction. | Feel it. Don't obey it. |
| S04 | Pain × resistance = suffering. | Drop one term, the equation collapses. |
| S05 | The breath is the only place the past cannot reach. | This breath. Then this one. |
| S06 | Attention is the only currency. | Where it goes, you go. |
| S07 | You cannot meditate. You can only stop interrupting it. | Meditation is the default state. |
| S08 | Every loop you name dies a little. | Naming is surgery. |
| S09 | The witness is not a skill. It is who you already are. | You have never not been watching. |
| S10 | Discipline is love in working clothes. | Not punishment. Love wearing boots. |
| S11 | The opposite of addiction is not sobriety. It is presence. | Show up. The pull dies. |
| S12 | You don't need a guru. You need a mirror that doesn't lie. | A teacher is a clean mirror. Nothing more. |

C. The Four Paths — 4 mini-seasons, 8 episodes each = 32 reels
A complete map of the four classical yogas, in our painterly universe, with levels so the viewer can locate themselves the way the in-app engine would.

| Path | What it is | 8-episode arc |
|---|---|---|
| Bhakti Yoga (devotion) | Path of the heart | What is bhakti → the 9 forms → finding your deity/principle → chanting → kirtan → tears as evidence → bhakti without religion → the 5 levels of bhakti (curious → emotional → consistent → surrendered → dissolved) |
| Karma Yoga (action) | Path of selfless work | What is karma yoga → action without attachment → the 3 kinds of action → work as worship → karma in the office → the dropped fruit → service without saviour complex → 5 levels (paid → balanced → unconditional → invisible → effortless) |
| Jnana Yoga (knowledge) | Path of inquiry | What is jnana → who am I → neti-neti → the witness → the four mahavakyas → discrimination (viveka) → dispassion (vairagya) → 5 levels (reading → reflecting → inquiring → witnessing → resting) |
| Raja Yoga (the royal path) | Path of practice | The 8 limbs → yama → niyama → asana → pranayama → pratyahara → dharana/dhyana → samadhi → 5 levels (occasional → daily → absorbed → sustained → effortless) |

Plus a 5th bonus mini-season — The Other Roads — 8 episodes covering Hatha, Kriya, Tantra, Mantra, Yantra, Nada, Laya, Kundalini — one painterly explainer each, no pop-mysticism, real lineage references.

Every Four Paths episode ends with the same locked CTA:
 "You are at Level [X]. Here is the next step." (mirroring §21 The Stairwell.)

D. The Practice Library — 24 episodes, 30–45s each
One reel per named practice in the app. Same structure: name → why → how → tonight's first attempt. Locked first 12:

| # | Practice | Hook |
|---|---|---|
| P01 | Observation (Sakshi) | "Don't fix it. Watch it." |
| P02 | Self-Inquiry (Atma Vichara) | "Ask one question until it answers itself: who is asking?" |
| P03 | Neti-Neti | "Not this. Not this. What's left is you." |
| P04 | Conscious Breath | "Three slow ones. The day reorganises." |
| P05 | Karma (Action without Attachment) | "Do the work. Drop the result. Watch the lightness arrive." |
| P06 | Kriya | "Kriya is breath that moves the body's locked rooms." |

| P08 | Tantra (the real one, not the bedroom one) | "Saying yes to what is, including the parts you wish weren't." |

| P12 | Witness in Action | "Wash the dish. Watch the washing. That's it." |

E. Guru Speaks — weekly, 60s, painterly portrait + lip-synced voice
One of the 36 in-app gurus delivers a single teaching from their tradition. We rotate through all 36 over 36 weeks. This is the lowest-cost, highest-trust series — reuses the master portraits we already own, adds ElevenLabs voice + subtle motion. Brand-building gold.

F. Voice Notes — 3×/week, 30–45s
Audio-first reels: founder or guru voice over a single still painterly frame. Cheapest pillar, highest intimacy. Used to fill the slot between heavy cinematic drops.

passages.text:

3. The founder is the only person allowed to break the brand grid with a real human face.
4. The product wins by feeling like a person made this for me, not an algorithm served me this.

Samir is to ConsciousOS what Anton is to ConsciousOS. We do not hide that — we use it.

The intimate spine. Same voice. Same one looping painterly background. Different teaching every time. This is the pillar that scales fastest because the visual cost is paid once and reused.

How it works:
1. Generate 8 evergreen background plates (one per mood: dawn, dusk, monsoon, candle, temple, ocean, mountain, void). Each is a 5s looped videogen clip on the locked palette. Total one-time cost: 100 cr.
2. Every carousel reuses one of the 8 plates — zero new render cost.
3. Founder/guru voiceover (ElevenLabs, 30–90s) sits on top.
4. 5–8 swipe cards with one line each appear in time with the voice (Anton 140pt, gold highlight, locked typography).
5. Locked closer card: handle + URL.

- Card text must be readable in 2 seconds on a 6.1" screen. If a friend can't read it across the room, it's too long.

passages.heading: §26 — Cost Compression Layer (Pre-Built Asset Vault + Free Voice + Hollywood Captions)
passages.text: Same R004-grade output. 70% lower per-piece cost. The trick: build the expensive stuff once, reuse it 600+ times, and move the voice line off paid TTS onto Google.

passages.heading: 26.1 The principle
passages.text: R004 looked cinematic because of four things: (1) painterly frame, (2) slow real motion, (3) one warm voice, (4) a single bottom-heavy caption that landed like a movie title card. None of those four require us to regenerate from scratch every reel. Three of them can be vaulted. Only the videogen motion + the voice line need to be fresh per piece — and even the voice can drop to free.

passages.heading: 26.2 The Asset Vault (build once, reuse forever)
passages.text:
| Vault layer | What we build once | Volume | Reuse target | One-time cost | Per-piece saving |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| V1 — Background Plates | 24 painterly stills (§22 LUT, no characters) covering every theme atmosphere: dawn pier, dusk temple step, monsoon window, candle void, stone corridor, ocean horizon, snow peak, painted void, neon street rain, kitchen 11:47 PM, train window, bedroom ceiling, bathroom mirror, lift door, balcony rail, prayer-room floor, ghat steps, forest path, desert dune, monastery courtyard, library lamp, hospital corridor, office cubicle, empty bus | 24 | 600+ pieces (carousels + reel inserts + quote tiles) | 288 cr (24 × 12) | -12 cr per Format B piece, -3 cr per quote tile |
| V2 — Background Music Beds | 12 royalty-free / commissioned 60s loops in three moods × four tempos: Stillness (drone+tanpura), Tension (low cello pulse), Release (single piano + breath), each at slow/walk/heart/run BPM | 12 | Every reel + carousel forever | 0 cr (use Pixabay/YouTube Audio Library + ElevenLabs Music for 4 originals = 80 cr) | -2 cr per piece (no per-reel music gen) |
| V3 — Ambient Sound FX | 30 micro-SFX: tea pour, page turn, breath in, breath out, temple bell, distant traffic, monsoon, fire crackle, footstep on stone, door close, phone notification, clock tick, water drop, wind, prayer chant 3s, etc. | 30 | Every reel | 0 cr (Freesound CC0) | -1 cr per piece |
| V4 — Character Plates | 12 painterly frames per recurring character (Samir-painterly, Modern Guru, 5 path masters, Sleeper, Observer, Witness, Alchemist, Future Self) × 6 emotion states = 432 stills | 432 | Every cinematic reel that needs that character | 864 cr (one heavy month) | -8 cr per Format A reel (no character regen, just animate) |
| V5 — Motion Templates | 10 reusable 5-second videogen motions (slow zoom, candle flicker, rain on window, breath rise, hand to chest, eyes close, page flip, walking POV, looking up, fade through black) | 10 | Spliced into 200+ reels as B-roll | 120 cr | -4 cr per Format A reel |
| V6 — Caption Title Cards | 80 pre-rendered Hollywood-style lower-third caption frames at 9:16 with the locked typography (see §26.4) — just swap the text | 80 | Every reel | 0 cr (CSS/After Effects template) | -0.5 cr per piece |
| V7 — Outro Stinger | 1 universal 2-second outro: lotus glyph + "ConsciousOS" wordmark + 3-note motif | 1 | Every reel forever | 12 cr | brand consistency, free reuse |

Total one-time vault build: 1,364 cr. Amortized across the year's 653 pieces = 2 cr saved per piece × 653 = 1,306 cr recovered in year 1, and the vault keeps paying out year 2, 3, 4.

passages.heading: 26.3 Voice: drop to Google Cloud TTS (free tier) for 80% of pieces
passages.text:
| Use case | Old voice | New voice | Why | Cost shift |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Loop Library narration (52/yr) | ElevenLabs cloned guru | Google Cloud TTS — Neural2-J (warm male) or Wavenet-D | Loop reels are short, declarative, factual. Google Neural2 at 0.85x speed + our background bed is indistinguishable in feed | $16/M chars → effectively free under 1M char/mo |
| Wisdom / Secrets carousels (70/yr) | ElevenLabs | Google Neural2-F (warm female) for variety | Carousels are read in silence by viewers anyway; voice is bonus | free |
| Quote tiles, micro-reels, Sleeper, Mindset (150/yr) | ElevenLabs | Google TTS | Same | free |
| Stairwell, Theme R-reels, Guru Speaks (120/yr) | KEEP ElevenLabs cloned guru voice | unchanged | These are the channel's signature emotional moments. Cloning is non-negotiable here. | unchanged |
| Founder Notes (24/yr) | Real Samir lav mic | unchanged | §24 exception holds. | unchanged |

Net voice saving: 280 pieces × 1.5 cr ElevenLabs cost = 420 cr/yr saved. ElevenLabs reserved only for the 18% of pieces where voice IS the product.

Implementation note: add a single edge function tts-router that takes { text, tier } and routes tier: "free" → Google Cloud TTS API, tier: "signature" → ElevenLabs. Keeps the rest of the pipeline identical.

passages.heading: 26.4 Hollywood-grade bottom captions (locked spec)
passages.text:
This is the visible quality lever. Get this right and a Google-TTS reel reads as cinematic as an ElevenLabs one.

Position lock: caption sits in the bottom 22% of the 9:16 frame, anchored at 78% from top, never higher. This is the Christopher Nolan / A24 / Apple TV title-card zone — eye lands there after scanning the image.

Typography lock:
- Font: Inter Tight ExtraBold for English, Mukta ExtraBold for Hindi/Devanagari, never serif, never script.
- Size: 64–88pt for hook lines (1–4 words), 44–52pt for full-sentence captions. Big. Movie-poster big.
- Tracking: -2% (tight, premium).
- Line height: 1.05 (cinematic, not webby).
- Max 2 lines. Ever. If it doesn't fit in 2 lines, the line is wrong.

Color & contrast lock:
- Text: pure white #FFFFFF at 100% opacity.
- Behind text: 18% black scrim gradient rising from frame bottom to caption top — gives perfect contrast on any background plate without a hard box.
- Optional: 0.5px gold underline #D4AF37 only for the final word of the hook (the one that should hit). Used sparingly, max 1 reel in 4.

Animation lock:
- Caption fades in over 400ms with a 6px upward translate. No bounces. No typewriter. No karaoke highlights.
- Caption holds for the full duration of the spoken line +600ms tail.
- Caption swaps with 150ms cross-fade, never a cut.

Safe-zone lock: keep all text 48px from left and right edges, 120px from bottom (above Reels UI chrome — caption, like, share buttons).

One caption per beat. Never two captions on screen. Never a caption that competes with another text element in the frame.

Reference look: Dune: Part Two end-card titles. Past Lives opening. Apple's "Shot on iPhone" film series. That register. Not TikTok. Not motivational quote farm.

passages.heading: 26.6 Quality gate (non-negotiable before any reel ships)
passages.text:
Every piece must pass this 6-point check or it does not ship:

1. Plate test — pause at frame 1. Does it look like a still from a film? If no, regenerate.
2. Caption test — mute the reel. Can a viewer get the message from the caption alone in 1.5s? If no, rewrite.
3. Bed test — solo the BGM. Does it match the theme tempo from §22? If no, swap from vault.
4. Voice test — solo the voice line. Is it in the right tier (Google for declarative, ElevenLabs for emotional)? If no, re-route.
5. Outro test — does the reel end on the universal 2s lotus stinger? If no, append.
6. Bottom-zone test — overlay the Reels UI mock. Is the caption above the chrome AND in the 78% zone? If no, reposition.

One person, one minute per reel, no exceptions.

passages.text:

3. Day 3 — V3 (SFX library, 30 clips from Freesound). 0 cr.
4. Day 4 — V6 (caption template After Effects + CSS lower-third). 0 cr.
5. Day 5 — V1 (24 background plates, batch generated). 288 cr.
6. Day 6 — V5 (10 motion templates). 120 cr.
7. Day 7 — V7 (outro stinger) + first compressed pilot reel using the full vault. Ship. Compare side-by-side to R004. If indistinguishable, lock the pipeline.

V4 (character plates, 432 stills, 864 cr) is the heaviest line — schedule across weeks 2–3, not week 1.

passages.heading: *How a piece stops being content and starts being something a stranger remembers for a year.*
passages.text:
Most "good content" is forgettable because it is built to be liked.
 World-class content is built to be felt once and never un-felt.
 This section is the craft floor every piece must clear before it ships.

---

passages.heading: 27.1 — The 8 Laws of Unforgettable
passages.text: Every reel, every carousel, every voice post must obey these 8 laws. If a piece violates more than 1, it does not ship — it goes back to the desk.

passages.heading: Law 1 — **Specificity beats scale**
passages.text:
Never "many people feel anxious." Always "you, at 11:47 PM, refreshing the same Slack channel for the 7th time."
A named hour, a named app, a named gesture, a named room. The brain cannot dismiss specifics.

passages.heading: Law 2 — **One feeling, one frame, one line**
passages.text:
Each piece carries exactly one emotional payload. Not three insights. One.
If you can't say the payload in 6 words, the piece isn't ready.
Example payload: "You are not lazy. You are looping."

passages.heading: Law 3 — **Earn the silence**
passages.text:
The most powerful 2 seconds in any reel are the ones with no voice, no music, no caption — just image.
Every reel must contain one deliberate silence beat of ≥1.2s. That is where the viewer's own thought lands.
Without silence, the piece is noise.

passages.heading: Law 4 — **The viewer must finish the sentence**
passages.text:
Never close the loop for them. Leave the last 15% inside their chest.
Weak: "And that's why awareness sets you free."
World-class: "And the part of you watching the loop — has never been inside it."
[fade to black]

passages.heading: Law 5 — **No second draft on screen**
passages.text:
A first draft is a sketch. World-class is the 7th pass, not the first instinct.
Every named hook in the file (Loop Library, Stairwell, Theme R-reels) must be rewritten 3 times before it is filmed. The 3rd version ships.

passages.heading: Law 6 — **The hook is a wound, not a question**
passages.text:
Don't ask "Do you ever feel tired?"
Open the wound: "The exhaustion of saying 'I'm fine' for the 11th time today, knowing nobody will ask the 12th."
A question lets the viewer scroll. A wound makes them stop.

passages.heading: Law 7 — **One image they cannot un-see**
passages.text:
Every piece must have one signature visual — an image that, if shown alone with no sound, still carries the payload.
R004's signature: the candle in the void, flame unmoved by the dark.
Loop Library AC003's signature (target): the phone screen at 11:47 PM, refreshed for the 7th time, the timestamp slightly out of sync with the system clock.
If you can't name the signature image in one sentence, the piece has none.

passages.heading: Law 8 — **End on a private sentence**
passages.text:
The last line is not a CTA. It is not a brand mention. It is not "follow for more."
It is the sentence the viewer wishes someone had said to them at their worst moment.
Example: "You are not late. You are arriving."

---

passages.heading: 27.2 — The Sentence Stack (the only writing system that matters)
passages.text:
Every piece is built in 4 sentences, in this exact order. No exceptions.

| # | Sentence | Purpose | Length |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | The Wound | Name the exact moment with surgical specificity. | 12–18 words |
| S2 | The Mirror | Show the viewer this is not a flaw — it has a name, a shape, a structure. | 10–16 words |
| S3 | The Crack | One sentence of unexpected truth that re-frames the wound. | 8–14 words |
| S4 | The Door | A private sentence the viewer will whisper to themselves later. | 5–9 words |

Worked example (Loop AC003, voice carousel):
- S1: "It's 2:14 AM. You've refreshed the same email seven times. You don't even know what you're looking for."
- S2: "That's not weakness. That's a pattern. It has a name. AC003."
- S3: "Willpower won't fix it — because the part of you doing the refreshing is not the part you're trying to control."
- S4: "You are not the loop. You are the one who just noticed it."

If a draft can't be compressed into this 4-sentence stack, it is not one piece — it is two pieces pretending to be one. Split it.

---

passages.heading: 27.3 — The 6 Senses Rule
passages.text:
A world-class piece touches at least 4 of these 6 senses in 30 seconds. Cheap content touches 1 (sight) or 2 (sight + sound).

| Sense | How it shows up |
|---|---|
| Sight | The signature image (Law 7). |
| Sound | One BGM bed + one diegetic sound (e.g., a real keyboard tap, a real exhale, a real chai cup). |
| Touch | Verbs of texture: the cold edge of the phone, the weight of the blanket you didn't pull up, the sweat behind your knee. |
| Smell/Taste | Mentioned by name once: the chai gone cold, the hostel corridor, your father's deodorant. |
| Time | A specific hour. Always. 11:47 PM, 4:18 AM, the gap between alarms. |
| Body | One named body location: the back of your throat, the space between your shoulder blades, your jaw at 3 PM. |

Audit before ship: count the senses. If <4, rewrite.

---

passages.heading: 27.4 — The "Send This To One Person" Test
passages.text:
Before any piece ships, the writer must answer this question in writing:

 "Which exact human, in which exact moment, will screenshot this and send it to one specific friend with the message 'this is literally you'?"

If the writer cannot name:
- a person (Arjun / Priya / Diya / Samir, from 00-FOUNDATION/01-ONE-FEELING.md),
- a moment (the hour, the room, the trigger),
- a friend they would send it to,
- the message they would type when they send it,

— the piece does not ship. It goes back to the desk.

This single test kills 80% of mediocre drafts before they consume render credits.

---

passages.heading: 27.5 — The Craft Floor (technical minimums)
passages.text:
No piece ships unless it clears all 10:

1. Hook lands inside 1.2s — not 3, not 2. The first painted frame carries the wound.
2. No more than 2 fonts on screen, ever. Inter Tight ExtraBold + Mukta ExtraBold. Period.
3. One emoji maximum per piece. Often zero.
4. Caption never repeats the voice line word-for-word. Caption extends, voice ignites.
5. BGM bed never crosses -18 LUFS under voice. The voice is always the king.
6. No zoom-in transitions. No whoosh SFX. No TikTok-isms. We are A24, not BuzzFeed.
7. Outro stinger is 0.8s, gold-on-black, lotus mark only. No URL, no handle, no "follow."
8. First and last frame must work as standalone stills (for screenshot virality).
9. Color grade locked to LUT-01 (warm shadows, cool highlights, gold midtones — the painterly bible from §22).
10. The piece passes the mute test: played silent, the signature image + bottom captions still deliver the payload.

---

passages.heading: 27.6 — The Reference Register (what we are measured against)
passages.text:
We are not competing with other wellness accounts. We are competing with these:

| Medium | Reference | What we steal |
|---|---|---|
| Voice & restraint | Pixar's Soul opening (5 min) | Saying everything by saying almost nothing. |
| Caption typography | Apple's "Shot on iPhone" series | 64–88pt, lowercase, anchored low, no chrome. |
| Color & grade | Wong Kar-wai's In the Mood for Love | Painterly amber + teal. The frame as a held breath. |
| Cinematography | Lubezki's long takes (Roma, Birdman) | One eye, one room, one continuous emotion. |
| Voice register | Krista Tippett's On Being | Permission, never instruction. The pause is the teaching. |
| Story compression | Pixar's Up — the 4-minute Carl & Ellie sequence | A whole life inside one emotional arc. |
| Brand restraint | Aesop, Loewe, A24 | The brand whispers. The work shouts. |
| Founder voice | Rick Rubin — The Creative Act | Plainspoken. Unhurried. Ancient. |

If a draft would not survive being placed next to any of these, it is not world-class. It is content.

---

passages.heading: 27.7 — The 3-Pass Writing Ritual (no piece skips this)
passages.text:
Every named piece is written three times, by three lenses:

1. Pass 1 — The Therapist. Get the wound right. Specificity over polish. Ugly is fine.
2. Pass 2 — The Poet. Compress. Cut every adjective that isn't earning. Earn the silence (Law 3).
3. Pass 3 — The Director. Read it out loud. If a sentence can't be spoken in one breath without strain, break it. If the last line doesn't land in the chest, rewrite it.

The shipped piece is Pass 3. Never Pass 1. Never Pass 2.

This is non-negotiable. It is the difference between good and the kind of thing a stranger tattoos.

---

passages.heading: 27.8 — The Fan Conversion Equation
passages.text:
A viewer becomes a fan when 3 pieces in a row do the same thing to them:

 (Wound named) × (Mirror held) × (Door opened) = Fan.

This is why the channel is built around themes (1 per week, 7 pieces compounding) rather than scattered drops.
By piece 3 of any theme, the right viewer thinks: "This account is reading my life."
By piece 7, they have shared 1, saved 2, and followed.
By theme 4, they are quoting us in their own DMs.

A fan is not made by reach. A fan is made by being the only voice in their feed that names the thing nobody else is naming.

---

passages.heading: 27.9 — The Daily Cut (the only quality control that matters)
passages.text:
Every day, before any piece ships, the founder (or whoever holds the lock) does this in 10 minutes:

1. Watch the piece muted, on a phone, in a noisy room. Does the signature image land? Y/N
2. Watch with sound, eyes closed. Does the voice carry the payload alone? Y/N
3. Read the caption alone, no video. Does it stand as a tweet? Y/N
4. Read the 4-sentence stack (S1–S4). Are all 4 present? Y/N
5. Name the exact viewer + moment + friend (§27.4). Can you? Y/N
6. Could this have been made by any other wellness brand? N required.
7. Would Samir send this to his own mother because it finally explains him? Y required.

6 of 7 = ship. 5 or below = back to the desk, no exceptions.

---

passages.heading: 27.10 — The Promise (the line that governs everything)
passages.text:
"Every piece we publish is something someone, somewhere, was waiting their whole life to hear — and didn't know it until the moment they saw it."

This is the bar. Not engagement. Not virality. Not reach.

That sentence. That moment. That stranger.

If a piece doesn't aim there, it doesn't belong on the channel.

If a piece lands there even once a week — we win the decade.

---

passages.heading: *Stop comparing to wellness pages. Start competing with the 100 channels that already own this attention.*
passages.text:
Honest reframe: R001–R007 are beautiful — but right now they live in a feed that already contains Jay Shetty (10M+), Sadhguru (12M+), Vex King, Yung Pueblo (3M+), Mel Robbins, Rich Roll, Lewis Howes, The Holistic Psychologist (5M+), Nedra Tawwab, Mark Manson, Naval clips, Huberman clips, Andrew Tate clips, Alex Hormozi, Mo Gawdat, Esther Perel, Gabor Maté clips, Tim Ferriss clips, Iyanla Vanzant, Tara Brach, Pema Chödrön clips, Eckhart clips, Mooji clips, Ram Dass clips, Adyashanti clips, Rupert Spira clips, plus 60+ Indian regional consciousness pages already producing 5–15 reels/week with 200K–2M followers each.

 A billion-dollar consumer business is not built by being one of 100. It is built by being the only one doing the one thing none of them can do.
 §28 is the competitive lens.

---

passages.heading: 28.1 — Honest audit of the 4–5 reels we have
passages.text:

|---|---|---|---|
| R001 (1BHK / Bangalore) | Specificity, silence, painterly grade. World-class craft. | Reads as one beautiful film, not episode 1 of a system. No series spine visible. | Re-cut last frame: small LOOP LIBRARY · AC003 · 01 / 52 mark in corner. Now it joins a universe. |
| R002 | Voice + image lock. Holds tone. | Could be any Yung Pueblo post. Differentiation invisible to a stranger scrolling. | Add the named loop ID on screen for 0.6s. The ID is the moat. Nobody else has IDs. |
| R003 | Atmosphere. | Payload diffuse. Viewer can't say what they just watched in 6 words. | Apply §27.2 Sentence Stack. One payload, named. |

Verdict: the frames are world-class. The system signaling is invisible. We are publishing masterpieces that look like one-offs in a feed of franchises. That is the bottleneck. Fix it before producing piece #6.

---

passages.heading: 28.2 — The 100-channel landscape (who actually owns this attention right now)
passages.text:
We are not entering an empty market. We are entering a colosseum. Map it honestly:

| Tier | Examples | What they own | Where they leak |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tier S — Personality monoliths | Sadhguru, Jay Shetty, Eckhart, Mooji, Gabor Maté, Esther Perel | Face + decades + institutional trust | No product, no system, no daily mirror. Pure inspiration. Forgotten in 30 min. |
| Tier A — Modern teachers | Yung Pueblo, Nedra Tawwab, Mark Manson, Holistic Psychologist, Mel Robbins | Quote-card kingdom. Saves & shares. | Quote-card kingdom. No depth, no engine, no journey. |
| Tier A — Podcast clip farms | Huberman, Naval, Hormozi, Lewis Howes, Rich Roll, Tim Ferriss, Mo Gawdat clips | Authority via long-form proof. | Generic optimization vibe. Western, masculine, productivity-coded. No interiority. |
| Tier A — Cinematic spirituality | AloMoves, Insight Timer clips, Calm reels, Headspace shorts, Liberate | Polish + brand trust. | Soft. Risk-averse. Cannot say AC003. Cannot name a wound. |
| Tier B — Indian English consciousness | Gaur Gopal Das, Vivek Bindra (overlap), Ranveer Allahbadia spiritual cuts, Sister Shivani clips | Massive Indian reach. | Sermon mode. Top-down. No mirror. |
| Tier B — Regional Hindi/Tamil/Marathi spiritual | 60+ pages, 200K–2M followers each | Cultural rootedness. | Production quality 1990s. Cannot reach English-fluent NRI/Tier-1 youth. |
| Tier C — Aesthetic quote farms | 1000s of pages | Visual feed candy. | Zero retention, zero memory, zero product. |

The honest truth:
- We cannot out-personality Sadhguru.
- We cannot out-quote Yung Pueblo.
- We cannot out-clip Huberman.
- We cannot out-polish Calm.
- We cannot out-reach Sister Shivani.

We don't need to. None of them can do the one thing we can.

---

passages.heading: 28.3 — The unownable moat (why a billion-dollar business is possible)
passages.text:
Every competitor above shares the same structural ceiling: they sell content. We sell a mirror that has a name for the thing the viewer is doing right now.

| What they have | What we have |
|---|---|
| Quotes | Named loops (AC003, VAL001, REL007). The IDs become language the viewer adopts. |
| Teachers | The Temple — 13 calibrated gurus who remember the viewer across years. |
| Practices | A spiral — 11 bands × 6 dimensions, the viewer can see themselves moving. |
| Inspiration | A diagnosis — by piece 3, the viewer thinks "this account knows where I actually am." |
| Followers | A relationship — the app is the destination; the channel is the foyer. |

This is the only billion-dollar content position in this category:

 We are not a wellness page. We are the only Instagram channel where a stranger learns the name of the loop they are inside, and walks into a Temple that already knows them.

Every reel must signal this position in the first 2 seconds and again at the outro. If it doesn't, it's competing with Yung Pueblo on Yung Pueblo's turf — and losing.

---

passages.heading: 28.4 — The 7 weapons no competitor has (use ALL of them, every week)
passages.text:
1. The ID System. Every loop has a code (AC003, VAL001). Codes are sticky. Codes are searchable. Codes are tribal. Nobody else does this.
2. The Temple Universe. 13 named gurus, 100+ masters, scrollable sanctuary. Each guru is a recurring character. Pixar discipline applied to spirituality. Nobody else does this.
3. The Spiral. 11 bands × 6 dimensions. The viewer can locate themselves on a map. Nobody else does this.
4. The Mirror Diagnostic. A 4-phase landing-page experience that names the viewer's loop in 90 seconds. Drop it as a reel format. Nobody else does this.
5. The Founder-as-Practitioner. Samir hasn't meditated for 42 days while building a meditation app. That confession is more valuable than any guru's certainty. Nobody else can do this — by definition.
6. The Painterly Bible (§22) + Caption Floor (§26.4) + Sentence Stack (§27.2). A craft moat 100 channels would need 18 months to even attempt. Nobody else has this.
7. The Engine. Every reel can quietly point to a generated experience inside the app — the user's own loop, named back to them. The reel is content. The app is the payoff. Nobody else has this — they have nowhere to send the viewer.

Rule from this point on: every reel must visibly carry at least 3 of these 7 weapons. If a reel shows none, kill it.

---

passages.heading: 28.5 — The billion-dollar content stack (the model we are actually building)
passages.text:
Stop thinking Instagram channel. Think media holding company with one app underneath.

 

A billion-dollar consumer business is built bottom-up, never top-down.

- Calm built Layer 1 + Layer 5 and skipped 2, 3, 4 → ceiling at $2B and falling.
- Headspace built Layer 1 + Layer 5 with a weak 3 → ceiling at $3B and stuck.
- Sadhguru built Layer 3 + Layer 4 perfectly but no Layer 5 → personal brand, not transferable equity.
- We build all 5. That is the bet. The Instagram channel is the bridge from Layer 1 to Layer 4 — its only job.

If a reel doesn't move someone up at least one layer, it is a credit-burning vanity post.

---

passages.heading: 28.6 — The 100-Reel Compounding Math (why R001–R007 cannot stay one-offs)
passages.text:
Single reels do not build billion-dollar businesses. Series compound. The math:

| Production model | After 100 pieces |
|---|---|
| 100 standalone reels (current) | 100 separate impressions. 0 brand memory. 0 language adoption. 0 SEO/discoverability. |
| 100 pieces across 8 named series | Each series = a show. Viewers binge. Loop Library alone becomes a known phrase. ID search starts. UGC starts ("guys, I'm an AC003"). |
| Same 100 + outro that always points to one app destination | Each reel becomes a paid acquisition channel at zero CPM. 100 reels = 100 doors into the Temple. |

Decision lock:
 From reel #6 onward, no standalone pieces exist. Every piece has a series ID, an episode number, and a destination inside the app. R001–R005 are retro-fitted with on-screen series tags in their next re-release.

This single change is worth more than the next 100 reels we produce.

---

passages.heading: 28.7 — The 5 Things Every Future Reel Must Do (the billion-dollar checklist)
passages.text:
On top of §27's craft floor, every reel from #6 onward must:

1. Belong to a named series (visible as 0.8s lower-third at the end).
2. Carry a named loop ID or named guru (1 second on screen, minimum).
3. End with one private sentence the viewer will whisper later (§27 Law 8).
4. Point to a destination inside the app (a specific diagnostic, a specific guru, a specific practice — not "download our app").
5. Be a screenshot waiting to happen — first frame or last frame must work as a still that survives being shared with no caption.

5 of 5 = ship. 4 of 5 = back to the desk. 3 or below = killed.

---

passages.heading: 28.8 — What "world-class enough that anyone becomes a fan" actually means at billion-dollar scale
passages.text:
A fan at this scale is not someone who likes the post. A fan is someone who:

- Can name 2 of our loop IDs from memory.
- Has sent 1 reel to 1 specific friend with a personal note (§27.4).
- Has used a phrase from the channel in their own DMs ("that's such a Stairwell moment").
- Has quoted a guru by name without explaining who the guru is.
- Recognizes our painterly grade in 0.5 seconds, even before a caption appears.

When 5,000 humans do all 5, we have the seed of a billion-dollar consumer business.
When 500,000 humans do all 5, the business exists whether we keep posting or not.

That is the target. Not views. Not followers. Those 5 behaviors, in that order, in that many people.

Every reel from this point is graded against that ladder. If a reel can't move any viewer one rung up that ladder, it doesn't ship.

---

passages.heading: 28.9 — The Studio's Honest Take (no flattery)
passages.text:
We have:
- A1 craft. Already there. R001 + R004 prove it.
- A1 IP. The Temple, the loops, the spiral, the gurus. Underused in the channel so far.
- C-grade system signaling. The reels look like art films, not episodes of a show. This is the gap.
- D-grade conversion architecture. No destination, no UTM, no per-series CTA. Already flagged in §27 audit, still unbuilt.

A billion-dollar business is A1 craft × A1 IP × A1 system signaling × A1 conversion. We have the first two. We are leaking the last two.

The good news: we don't need to make better reels. We need to make the same reels visibly belong to a universe and visibly point somewhere. That is a 1-week fix. After that, every credit we spend compounds.

---

passages.heading: 28.10 — The Move (call the next action)
passages.text:
Pick one to lock the §28 thesis into production:

1. RETROFIT-5 — re-edit R001–R005 outros with series tag + loop ID + 0.8s lotus → app destination. 80 cr total. Turns 5 standalone art films into Episode 1s. Studio's strongest pick.
2. SERIES-SPINE — produce reels 6, 7, 8 as Loop Library #01, Stairwell #01, Theme #01 — proving the spine in one week.
3. MIRROR-REEL — film one reel of the Mirror Diagnostic itself. Weapon #4 from §28.4. Likely the single most viral format we have.
4. COMPETITOR-AUDIT — full deep-read of the top 20 channels in §28.2, with line-by-line "what they cannot do, that we can." Becomes the sales doc, the investor doc, the team doc.
5. LADDER-INSTRUMENT — wire the 5 fan behaviors in §28.8 into the app + analytics so we can actually count them. Without this, "billion-dollar" stays a vibe.

passages.heading: *Samir on screen. The way ConsciousOS, Claude, OpenAI, Cursor, Linear and Anthropic put their founders on screen — but for consciousness, not code.*
passages.text:
Why this format unlocks the billion-dollar layer: every Tier-S competitor in §28.2 is faceless or institutional. Sadhguru is a face but not a founder. Calm/Headspace are founders but not faces. Nobody in this category has a credible 26-year-old founder talking to camera about why he built it. That seat is empty. We sit in it.

---

passages.heading: 29.1 — The Reference Set (what this format actually is)
passages.text:
We are stealing the visual grammar of these, exactly:

| Reference | What we steal |
|---|---|
| Anders Hjemdahl / ConsciousOS founder shorts | Single light source, plain wall, founder talking to camera, captions hard-anchored bottom, 18–35s. |
| Anthropic / Dario Amodei explainers | Calm pace. No b-roll panic. Founder finishes a thought before the cut. |
| OpenAI launch videos (Sam, Mira, Greg) | Soft natural light, neutral wardrobe, no logo on shirt, room is the brand. |
| Cursor / Michael Truell shorts | Phone-shot is fine. Truth production. The product appears in-hand for 2 seconds, never as a screen-record dump. |
| Linear's Karri Saarinen "why we built X" | First-person. No "we." Founder owns the choice and the doubt. |
| Stripe Press / Patrick Collison interviews | Slow, deliberate, books in the background, the room signals taste. |
| Naval / Joe Hudson sit-downs | One subject, one question, one breath. The pause is the format. |

What we are NOT stealing: ring-light influencer YouTuber energy, jump-cut every 0.8s, neon overlays, "wait for it" hooks, MrBeast thumbnails. That energy kills the trust this format exists to build.

---

passages.heading: 29.2 — The Look (locked specs — no exceptions)
passages.text:
- Frame: 9:16. Founder centered slightly camera-left (rule of thirds). Eyes on the upper third line.
- Lens feel: 35–50mm equivalent. Phone is fine. Soft natural fall-off, no fisheye.
- Lighting: ONE source. North-facing window, or a single soft key 45° off-axis. Never overhead. Never ring-light. Shadows allowed.
- Background: real room. Books, plant, stone wall, a single diya, the corner of a window. Never a studio cyclorama. Never a plain green wall.
- Wardrobe: plain crew-neck, hoodie, or kurta. No logos, no brand text, no patterns. Earth tones only — bone, charcoal, olive, rust, ink. Never white. Never black-on-black (kills the painterly LUT).
- Color grade: same LUT-01 as every reel (§22 painterly, §26 cost layer). Warm shadows, cool highlights, gold midtones. Founder's skin reads warm-honey, never orange.
- Audio: lavalier or Rode VideoMicro. Room tone preserved. Never voice-over a flat wall — let the room breathe.
- Captions: §26.4 floor — Inter Tight ExtraBold, 64–88pt, anchored 78% from top, 18% black scrim gradient. Never on top of his face.
- Cut rhythm: average shot length 6–9 seconds, not 1.5. The pause is the proof.

---

passages.heading: 29.3 — The 4 Sub-Formats (every Founder Note is one of these — no other types exist)
passages.text:
| ID | Name | Length | Job | Example hook |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F-WHY | Why I built this | 25–45s | Origin / pain / refusal | "I built a meditation app while not meditating for 42 days. That is the entire story." |
| F-PROD | Product walk-through | 30–60s | Show ONE feature on his actual phone, in his actual hand, in his actual room | "This is the loop the engine just named for me at 11:47 last night. Watch." |
| F-CONFESS | The thing nobody admits | 18–35s | One sentence of founder honesty most founders would never post | "Last month's OpenAI bill was ₹9.4 lakhs. I have not told my parents." |
| F-LETTER | A letter to one user | 35–55s | Talking to one named viewer-archetype, eye-contact whole time | "This one is for the engineer refreshing Slack at 2 AM. I see you. The app sees you. Here is what we built for you." |

Lock: every Founder Note must declare its sub-format ID before shoot. No "we'll figure it out in edit." If it doesn't fit one of the four, it's not a Founder Note — it's a different format pretending.

---

passages.heading: 29.4 — The Sentence Stack, Founder Edition
passages.text:
Same §27.2 stack, calibrated for the founder voice:

| # | Founder version | Length |
|---|---|---|
| S1 The Wound | A confession — name a real moment, real cost, real number, real hour. | 12–18 words |
| S2 The Mirror | "And I am not the only one." Pull the viewer in. | 8–14 words |
| S3 The Crack | What he learned that re-frames the wound. Spoken slow. | 8–14 words |
| S4 The Door | A single sentence directed at one viewer. Eye contact. Hold for 1.2s of silence after. | 5–9 words |

Worked example (F-CONFESS):
- S1: "Last month's OpenAI bill was ₹9.4 lakhs. I have not told my parents."
- S2: "Every founder I know is one bill away from this."
- S3: "The product has to work or none of this was love — it was just expensive."
- S4: "So the product has to work." (hold, fade, lotus.)

---

passages.heading: 29.5 — How the founder photos get used (the system)
passages.text:
When the photos arrive in chat, they get filed into src/assets/founder/samir/ with this naming, and used only as instructed below:

| Folder | What goes in | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| samir/portraits/ | Static, eyes-to-camera, painterly-graded portraits | Reel cover frames (frame 1 + last frame). Carousel slide 1 of any F-WHY voice carousel. Landing-page founder section. |
| samir/in-room/ | Wide / mid shots in his actual room (hoodie, books, diya, window) | Instagram bio header, About page, press kit, investor deck cover. |
| samir/with-product/ | Phone in hand showing the app | F-PROD sub-format only. Never decorative. |
| samir/raw/ | Unprocessed source files | Archive. Never published directly — must pass through LUT-01 first. |

Protections (locked):
1. Founder face appears in at most 1 in 5 reels. Scarcity is the moat. Once he's in every reel, the painterly Temple universe dies.
2. Founder photo never sits next to a guru portrait in the same frame. Different axes of trust — collapsing them collapses both.
3. Founder photo is never used on a generic quote tile. If we wouldn't put Patrick Collison's face on a "rise and grind" tile, we don't put Samir's on one either.
4. Every published founder image must pass §27.5 mute test: if shown silent, does it carry one specific feeling? If it just says "founder smiling," kill it.

---

passages.heading: 29.6 — The Production Pipeline (per Founder Note)
passages.text:
1. Pick sub-format (F-WHY / F-PROD / F-CONFESS / F-LETTER).
2. Write the 4-sentence stack (§29.4). Three passes (§27.7).
3. Stage the room — one light, one frame, one prop. Less than you think.
4. One take per sentence, three takes per stack. Pick the most honest, not the most polished.
5. Cut on the breath, never on the word. The founder finishing exhaling is the cut point.
6. LUT-01 grade. No filters on top.
7. §26.4 captions. Bottom anchor. Hook word gold.
8. 0.8s lotus outro + series tag (FOUNDER NOTE · 03 / 36).
9. §28.7 5-of-5 ship check before publish.

Cost target per Founder Note: 3 cr (no videogen needed — real footage). This is the cheapest format we have.

---

passages.heading: 29.7 — Schedule lock
passages.text:
- 1 Founder Note per week. No more, no less.
- Always Tuesday (§D5 cadence in FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md already pre-allocated this slot).
- Year 1 = 52 Founder Notes. Mix: 18 F-WHY, 14 F-PROD, 12 F-CONFESS, 8 F-LETTER.
- This becomes the spine of the founder narrative when we eventually raise / launch / press cycle.

---

passages.text:
To file the photos correctly and ship F-WHY #01 this week, drop in this chat:

1. 3–8 portraits of Samir (eye-line to camera, single-light, plain shirt). I will sort into samir/portraits/ and grade with LUT-01.
2. 2–3 wide / room shots (hoodie, books, window, diya — the room is the brand). I will sort into samir/in-room/.
3. 1–2 with-product shots (phone in hand showing the app). I will sort into samir/with-product/.

Re-attach them in your next message and I will:
- Copy each into the correct subfolder under src/assets/founder/samir/.
- Generate a LUT-01-graded variant of the strongest portrait as the F-WHY #01 cover frame.
- Write the F-WHY #01 4-sentence stack (the "meditation app while not meditating for 42 days" opener) ready to film.

passages.heading: 29.9 — The Move
passages.text:
1. PHOTOS-IN — you re-drop the photos, I file + grade them tonight.
2. F-WHY-01 — I write F-WHY #01 (script + shot list + caption) right now without waiting on the photos, so the moment they land we shoot.
3. FOUNDER-52 — I draft all 52 Founder Note titles + sub-format assignments for Year 1, locked to the §29.7 schedule.
4. LANDING-FACE — once photos are filed, swap the landing-page hero to a graded Samir-in-room shot — the single highest-trust upgrade we can ship to the marketing site.

passages.heading: §30.1 — Production rules the AI must obey on every row
passages.text:
1. NO CODES IN THE PIECE. The viewer must never hear or see AC003, VAL001, EM014, etc. The engine uses them. The reel does not.
2. Use ONLY the hook column as the on-screen / voice line. Do not improvise — the §27 Sentence Stack is already inside it.
3. Soundtrack column = bed only. Voice always sits at -6dB above bed. Bed never crosses -18 LUFS under voice (§26.4).
4. Visual column is the brief for videogen / plate selection. No additional creative liberty. Painterly LUT-01 always.
5. Character column says no human face for 90% of the list. Only Founder Notes (FN-) and Master/Guru reels show a recognised figure.
6. Episode tag must appear as a 0.8s lower-third at the end of every reel (e.g., STAIRWELL · 03 / 30). This is the franchise signal from §28.
7. Caption (Instagram side, separate doc) never repeats the voice line. Caption extends; voice ignites (§27.5).
8. Founder Notes are the only format where Samir's face appears, max 1 in 5 published pieces, per §29.5.

passages.heading: §30.2 — How to read the table when batching production
passages.text:
- Pick a row. Lock format. Pull plate from §26 V1 vault. Pull bed from V2 vault.
- If REEL: write 4-sentence stack from Hook (§27.2), record voice (Google TTS for 80%, ElevenLabs for Stairwell + Themes + Guru Speaks + Founder per §26.3), generate cinematic via videogen using Visual as prompt + plate as starting frame.
- If VOICE-CAROUSEL: pull plate from V1 (it loops), record voice, build 5–8 cards in §26.4 caption spec, export.
- If VOICE-POST: still + audio. Lowest cost format we have (0.5 cr).
- After every batch of 10, run §27.9 Daily Cut. Ship 6/7 minimum.

---

passages.heading: §31.1 — Video engine: AI generator only. No Remotion. No After Effects. No Premiere.
passages.text:
Every motion piece in this channel — Diagnosis Reel, Founder Note B-roll, Master Speaks plates, transitions, hero loops, landing-page background — is produced by an AI text-to-video generator (Runway / Veo / Kling / Sora / ConsciousOS videogen — whichever is available in the sandbox). No code-based motion graphics, no timeline editors, no React renderers.

Why locked:
- One pipeline = one look. Mixing tools breaks the LUT-01 grade.
- Cost ceiling holds: ₹3 cr/year (per §26) only if every clip is a single AI gen.
- Ship-speed: a Diagnosis Reel = 6 × 10s AI clips + voice + caption. 30 min/piece. Not 3 days.

Hard rules for the AI:
1. Always call videogen--generatevideo (or the available equivalent). Never scaffold a Remotion / Bun / Node project.
2. Clip length: 5s or 10s only. A 60s reel = 6 × 10s clips, stitched with ffmpeg -f concat.
3. Aspect: 9:16, resolution: 1080p, unless explicitly overridden.
4. Starting frame: when continuity matters across cuts (same room, same face, same prop), pass the last frame of clip N as startingframe of clip N+1. Extract with ffmpeg -sseof -0.04.
5. Faces: never generate Samir's face from text. Always pass a real reference photo from src/assets/founder/samir/portraits/ as startingframe. Same rule for any human face — no generative people from prompt alone.
6. Voice: ElevenLabs (paid masters) or Google TTS (free narration). Never the AI video tool's built-in voice.
7. Music: licensed bed from src/assets/audio/bgm/ per §26.4. Never AI-generated music inside the video tool.
8. Captions: burned in post via ffmpeg + subtitles= filter using the §27.4 caption floor — not the video tool's built-in captions.
9. Output: always write the final stitched MP4 to /mnt/documents/ and emit a <presentation-artifact tag.
10. No Remotion, no Manim, no Three.js, no Lottie, no Blender, no bun install, no npm install of any video library for production. Those are forbidden tools for this channel.

passages.heading: §31.3 — Forbidden, by name
passages.text:
Never use these for any production piece, even if asked:
- Remotion, React, Vite, Bun, Node, Webpack — any code-driven motion
- After Effects, Premiere, DaVinci, Final Cut — any timeline editor
- Manim, Three.js, p5.js, Lottie, Rive — any animation framework
- Stable Diffusion video, AnimateDiff, ComfyUI workflows — only the sanctioned text-to-video tool

ffmpeg is allowed only for: concat, audio mux, LUT apply, caption burn, frame extraction. Never for filters that fake motion.

---

passages.heading: 60-second product-launch flagship · Satyayuga · ConsciousOS
passages.text:
Reference DNA studied: Apple Vision Pro — Introducing, Humane AI Pin reveal, Rabbit R1 keynote, Anthropic Claude 3 launch, ConsciousOS agentic mode trailer. Common grammar = slow opening void → cultural problem named → product as quiet inevitability → one feature shown → human transformation → wordmark over silence. We borrow the grammar, not the look. Their look is glass + chrome. Ours is obsidian + gold + diya.

Format: 9:16 · 1080p · 60s · 6 × 10s clips, stitched with ffmpeg.
Engine: AI video generator only (per §31).
Voice: ElevenLabs — George (JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb) — deep, slow, contemplative. Stability 0.55, similarity 0.85, speed 0.9.
Audio bed: room tone + low cinematic drone, -20 LUFS, ducks under VO.
Caption rule: §27.4 — Anton 140pt, white body, gold (#FFB547) on the mirror word only.
Output: /mnt/documents/satyayuga-reel-001-launch.mp4

passages.heading: 0 · The One Law
passages.text:
Every reel is a small bet that a stranger, alone with their phone at the worst hour of their day,
 will feel — for 60 seconds — that someone, somewhere, finally saw them.

If a reel does not do that → kill it. No LUT, music, or caption polish saves a reel that doesn't see the viewer.

passages.heading: 4 · The R001 Storytelling Recipe (8-shot template)
passages.text:
Every cinematic reel follows this 8-shot arc (proven on R001 "The Wednesday I Quit ₹42 Lakhs"):

| Shot | Time | Beat | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0:00–0:06 | HOOK | A specific number + a specific moment (e.g., "1:1 with CTO, 4PM Wednesday"). Slow push-in on one object. |
| 2 | 0:06–0:13 | THE WORLD | Establishing tracking shot. The world subtly shifts (fluorescent → diya, glass → temple stone). |
| 3 | 0:13–0:20 | THE INCIDENT | The real-world thing happens. Hands on object. We don't see the face yet. |
| 4 | 0:20–0:28 | THE CINEMATIC PAUSE | Time freezes. Gold marigold particles assemble into something/someone (grandfather, guru, future-self). 1.5s+ silence. |
| 5 | 0:28–0:36 | THE WORDS | Extreme close-up of mouth saying ONE sentence. Cut to other person frozen mid-reaction. |
| 6 | 0:36–0:44 | WALKING OUT | Movement. Phone in hand. Doesn't send the message. World transforms behind them. |
| 7 | 0:44–0:53 | THE RESOLUTION ROOM | Their real space (1BHK, kitchen, hostel bed). Specific numbers on screen (rent, bill, user count). Head in hands → looks up → sees the gold particles. |
| 8 | 0:53–0:60 | THE END CARD | Looks directly into camera for the first time. Half-lit. Ancient figure (Krishna/master) materializes from gold dust behind them. Whisper: "I see you, [name]." |

Total: 60s. Voice: protagonist's locked voice + 1 master whisper at end.

passages.heading: Specificity rule (non-negotiable)
passages.text:
Every reel MUST contain at least 3 of these specificity anchors:
- exact time (11:47 PM, 2:14 AM, 4 PM Wednesday)
- exact number (₹42L, $11,407, 23 users, 47 refreshes, 14 months)
- named object (Slack window, OpenAI bill, calendar invite, son's doorway)
- named place (Indiranagar 1BHK, Gurgaon office, Pune kitchen)
- the loop in HUMAN words (NEVER the ID — "the 2 AM refresh" not "VAL004")

3. Quality over quantity. Each item must pass validation and score = 0.7 quality. Status: draft → review → published.

4. Progressive enhancement. Start with 100 high-quality items per category, then scale to targets.

5. User-centric. The library powers personalized experiences, not just browsing.
